dossier.mission: Write a technical article about the latest trends in AI coding assistants for senior developers

claims.claim: Claude Code surpassed GitHub Copilot as the most-used AI coding tool by mid-2026, with 39% workplace adoption vs Copilot's 21%

sources.title: AI Coding Agents: Adoption Trends
Claude Code overtakes GitHub Copilot to top developers' AI coding tools

credibility.rationale: JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026 surveyed 15,000+ professional developers worldwide. Large sample size, reputable publisher, recent data.

claims.claim: Experienced open-source developers were measured 19% slower when using AI coding tools despite believing they were 20% faster

sources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
AI coding tools may not speed up every developer, study shows
AI Productivity Paradox: Senior Developers 19% Slower

credibility.rationale: Randomized controlled trial by METR with 16 experienced developers on real codebases. Pre-registered, rigorous methodology. Note: February 2026 follow-up narrowed deficit to ~4% slower as tools improved.

claims.claim: PR review times increased 91% for teams with high AI adoption, while PR volume jumped 47-98%, creating a review bottleneck

sources.title: Agentic Code Review
GitHub Copilot is generating more code than your team can review
AI Coding Assistants Haven't Sped up Delivery Because Coding Was Never the Bottleneck

credibility.rationale: Faros AI telemetry data from 10,000+ developers across 1,255 teams. Multiple independent sources corroborate. Large-scale observational data.

claims.claim: AI-generated code contains 2.74x more vulnerabilities than human-written code, with a 45% failure rate on secure coding benchmarks

sources.title: AI Productivity Paradox: Senior Developers 19% Slower
AI Writes 41% of Code. Only 29% of Devs Trust It

credibility.rationale: Veracode 2025 GenAI Code Security Report cited but not directly linked. Secondary sources. Needs primary source verification.

claims.claim: 90% of professional developers use AI coding agents at least once a week, and 73% of engineering teams use them daily

sources.title: Claude Code overtakes GitHub Copilot
Claude Code Statistics 2026

credibility.rationale: JetBrains Research survey data. Pragmatic Engineer Survey (906 developers, Feb 2026) corroborates. Large sample sizes.

claims.claim: Cursor faced major pricing backlash in June 2025 when it shifted from 500 requests/month to $20 credit-based billing, effectively halving value for heavy users

sources.title: Did Cursor Raise Prices? The 2025 Controversy Explained
Cursor AI Pricing In 2026

credibility.rationale: Multiple independent trackers monitoring cursor.com/pricing. CEO public apology documented. Well-documented controversy.

claims.claim: Senior developers ship ~2.5x more AI-generated code than juniors (32% vs 13% of shipped code being AI-generated)

sources.title: Vibe Shift in AI Coding: Senior Developers Ship 2.5x More Than Juniors

credibility.rationale: Fastly survey of 791 developers. Moderate sample size. Self-reported data may have bias.

claims.claim: GitHub Copilot coding agent created over 1 million pull requests between May and September 2025

GitHub Copilot Coding Agent Press Release

sources.title: What Happened to the AI Coding Editor?
Cognition's $250M Windsurf Acquisition
The 72-Hour Deal

credibility.rationale: Multiple corroborating sources. TechCrunch originally reported Google talent deal. Cognition confirmed acquisition. Well-documented timeline.

sources.title: Windsurf vs Cursor: Devin Desktop Rebrand, 40+ IDEs [2026]

sources.title: AI Productivity Paradox: Senior Developers 19% Slower

sources.title: AI Productivity Paradox: Senior Developers 19% Slower

credibility_assessment.assessment: Research is well-grounded in Tier 1-2 sources. The strongest claims (adoption rates, productivity paradox, pricing changes) have solid primary or credible secondary sourcing. Weaker areas include security statistics and revenue estimates which rely on secondary citations. The main risk is data freshness given rapid market evolution.

key_themes_for_article.description: Experienced developers are slower with AI tools despite feeling faster, due to review overhead and high standards
Claude Code's rapid rise, Copilot's decline, Cursor's pricing controversy, and Windsurf's acquisition
Code generation is no longer the constraint; review, verification, and integration are
Widespread distrust of AI code coexists with widespread adoption, creating verification gaps
Shift from request-based to credit-based billing creates unpredictability for developers
Evolution from autocomplete to multi-agent orchestration and macro-delegation

recommended_article_structure: Opening: The paradox of senior developers and AI (hook with METR study)
Market landscape: Who's winning and losing (Claude Code vs Copilot vs Cursor)
The productivity paradox deep-dive: Why seniors are slower
The review bottleneck: Where speed gains go to die
Pricing and platform risks: Cursor controversy, Windsurf acquisition
Best practices for senior developers: Verification, tiered review, context management
Future outlook: Agentic workflows, macro-delegation, market consolidation
